## Design

### 2026-11-02: started and did a lot of the schematics for Nibble.

**2.08h**

started and did a lot of the schematics for Nibble.
I ran into a few problems: a bunch of the HC chips weren't in the KiCad library, and my lazy bum was not bothered to import them, so i just used the LS ones, which are an older variant but basically have the same schematic, so it doesn't change too much.

Completed Binary counter and capacitor, the 7 resistors, as well as 112 diodes, which took a really long time,
The schematics were so big that i decided to switch to an A3 schematic.

Next also completed the schematics for the row and opcode decoders, XOR chip, and arithmetic logic unit, the MUX, output register and the accumulator too. that's pretty much it.

### 2026-11-07: worked more on the schematic, and completed the output LED pins, with 1k resistors, and also completed the jump logic. also, built the clock, which will be set to run 2 ticks per second, for simplicit

**2.13h**

worked more on the schematic, and completed the output LED pins, with 1k resistors, and also completed the jump logic. also, built the clock, which will be set to run 2 ticks per second, for simplicity.

Also, completed the reset switch in the schematic, which uses a capacitor, resistor and a switch all in one! finally, completed the wiring and stuff for the USB power receptacle with 5.1k resistors, which also marks the completion of the schematic!!! :)))

next, completed footprint assignment which was pretty easy. additionally, ran ERC and fixed up an issue with some ADD_N and SUB_N label or something, because it wasn't being used so i just deleted it off of U4. also did some part renaming since some were out of date.

![img_2](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/iPQiPBB3YAqPu4RFe838ZhRAebDnRFaL/3a35a134eb6ab5a76c3468f3da1505cb1436cabe69326360aec0ee12862fa8bb.png)

![img_3](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/iPQiPBB3YAqPu4RFe838ZhRAebDnRFaL/7088c22a984acaec3db2edaceefe1bfde164bc377beb67ebfef2a11b22a2c7a3.png)

also, began arranging the pcb, with placing u1, u2 and the usbc in the top left corner, and the clock next to that, putting capacitors next to them (its a bit confusing since all of them are generic "GND"s or "VCC"s but whatever. spaced out all the u components, and used a script in the scripting console to arrange all 112 diodes in the center of the board. arraanged u4-8 as well.

![img_4](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/iPQiPBB3YAqPu4RFe838ZhRAebDnRFaL/c02667c7956b48987ca5a72b01015b884f25ff4239a205380e131e946a8182f2.png)

### 2026-11-08: this session finished the arrangement of u9-10 and started wiring, using a grid for the rows a op/n's. did a matrix wiring, then realised that the right side was really messy,got most of the parts in.

**3.9h**

this session finished the arrangement of u9-10 and started wiring, using a grid for the rows a op/n's. did a matrix wiring, then realised that the right side was really messy,got most of the parts in. then, lapse decided to break when i was wiring the rest. put holes literally everywhere to fix gnd issues. Also, journaled a bit for README writing and looking for BOM parts on LCSC and JLCPCB for quotes.
